newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BOF's Trichet says council no threat to Euro-bank.
newsitem.headline: BOF's Trichet says council no threat to Euro-bank.

text.p: Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said a stability council proposed by France to accompany the Euro single currency would not threaten the independence of the future European Central Bank.

Trichet said the proposed council would coordinate policy among governments in the single currency and look after implementation of a budget discipline pact agreed by a European Union summit in Dublin in December.

"The council of stability is a way that the French government has entertained to be sure that the implementation of this stability pact will be good, and as good as possible," Trichet told Reuters Financial Television at the World Economic Summit.

The proposal has come under fire from Germany's Bundesbank, which fears it might be used to undermine the independence of the European Central Bank (ECB) that is due to start work with the launch of the single currency.

"My understanding is that this council of stability, which has been accepted by a number of governments in Europe, will have to coordinate and organise the closest cooperation possible between the governments which will be in the Euro-zone, without changing the (Maastricht) treaty," he said.
Trichet said the Maastricht Treaty terms ensured that the European Central Bank would be independent of politicians.
"The independence of the central bank is enshrined in the (Maastricht) treaty and there is absolutely no point that this independence could be hampered in any respect," Trichet said.
"The ECB will have the legacy of, say, the Bundesbank, the Bank of the Netherlands , Banque de France and others. So it seems to me that independence is not the problem."
